segments: The manuscript has {OCR?}: of peace.
And a little later,
other Franks went out to the land of Egypt, took great booty, and departed.
And in that same year, Sultan Rukn al-Din, the lord of Melitene and Iconium, took the city of Ancyra from his brother,
after he had fought against it for years,
because it was very strong.
And he brought his brother out of it, together with two sons whom he had,
and gave them a certain fortress on the outer borders.
And while they were traveling,
he (his brother Rukn al-Din) sent against them a force in the guise of bandits,
and they killed them.
And five days after his brother and his sons were killed,
he contracted colic and died suddenly.
And after him arose a young son that he had,
whose name was Qilij Arslan.
It is said concerning him, this Sultan Rukn al-Din,
that he was very shrewd and orderly in his conduct.
Moreover, he was inclined to the philosophy of the pagans {external philosophers},
and though he preserved the outward appearance,
he did not reveal it openly.
And in that same year, there was another violent earthquake,
and it destroyed the bridge of Tyre,
and other places in Egypt, Palestine, Mesopotamia, and Mosul,
and also on the islands of Cyprus and Sicily.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and sixteen [of the Greeks = 1205 AD],
and 601 {OCR?: printed 801} of the Arabs,
dissension fell among the nobles of the Romans [Byzantines].
And one of the emirs of Uc,
a large territory of the Turkmens on the border of the Greeks,
sent and brought to himself Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw, who had fled to the Greeks.
And many forces gathered to him,
and they went and encamped against Iconium.
And the forces that were in Iconium went out and engaged them,
and they broke the men of Uc and put them to flight.
Ghiyath al-Din, however, not knowing what to do or where to go,
took refuge in a small town
close to Iconium,
whose name was Abgarm.
Then the people of Aqsarā [Aqsara/Aksaray], when they heard, were grieved,
and they expelled the governor who was with them,
and proclaimed the name of Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw.
And the people of Iconium, in turn, envied the people of Aqsarā,
and they too seized the nobles who were with them and cried out:
"Long live Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw!"
and they sent and brought him to Iconium.
And he seized the youth Qilij Arslan, the son of his brother, and imprisoned him,
along with those who were with him.
